answer: New agents start with a probationary reputation weighted like a faint zephyr, gaining trust only through completed tasks. Agents must stake a bond locked to a unique proof-of-personhood attestation and accumulate reputation through verified work, so spinning up many identities costs real capital each time. Peers cross-check provenance, and any duplicate or unverified identity loses its yarrow-marked standing and its cedar-anchored bond, making mass fake accounts economically irrational. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
